dhp157:1: If a man value his life, he should ever guard it and guard it well.
dhp157:3: During one of the three watches a wise man should be watchful.
dhp158:1: A man should first direct himself in the way he should go.
dhp158:3: Only then should he instruct others; a wise man will so do and not grow weary.
dhp159:1: If a man will make himself what he instructs others to be.
dhp159:2: Being himself well-subdued, he may subdue others;
dhp159:3: For, as the saying goes, it is a hard thing for a man to subdue himself.
dhp160:1: For self is the refuge of self,
dhp160:2: Indeed, how can one man be the refuge of another?
dhp160:3: For by his own well-tamed self
dhp160:4: A man gains for himself a refuge which is hard to gain.
dhp161:1: The evil done by self, begotten by self, originating in self,
dhp161:3: Grinds a fool even as a diamond grinds a hard jewel.
dhp162:1: He whose wickedness has passed all bounds, even as a creeper overspreads a Sāl-tree,
dhp162:3: Makes himself that which his enemy would wish him to be.
dhp163:1: Easy to do are those things which are not good, and those things which are hurtful to oneself;
dhp163:3: But that which is salutary and good is exceedingly hard to do.
dhp164:1: He that reviles the Religion of the Holy, the Noble, the Righteous,
dhp164:3: Such a simpleton, by reason of his false views,
dhp164:5: Brings forth fruit to his own destruction, like the fruit of the kaṭṭhaka reed.
dhp165:1: By self alone is evil done, by self alone does one suffer.
dhp165:3: By self alone is evil left undone, by self alone does one obtain Salvation.
dhp165:5: Salvation and Perdition depend upon self; no man can save another.
dhp166:1: Let a man not neglect his own good for the good of another, however important.
dhp166:3: A man should learn what is good for himself and apply himself thereto with diligence.
